strategy.summary: Build pandas at buggy commit 23f61296bcbf with the PR test diff applied, then run only the uint64 tests in test_to_datetime.py and test_to_timedelta.py. On the buggy revision the scalar to_datetime and to_timedelta calls with uint64 max and unit='ns' return a wrapped value instead of raising, so pytest.raises reports DID NOT RAISE. On the fixed revision those raise OutOfBoundsDatetime/OutOfBoundsTimedelta and the coerce tests yield NaT.

build_commands: python -m pip install cython numpy==2.2.1 python-dateutil tzdata pytest
pinned_because: numpy 2.2.1: taken from issue #60677 INSTALLED VERSIONS, era-inferred and not a documented constraint; chosen because the numerical reproducer was observed against it and it is numerically relevant
pandas 2.2.3 from the issue output is NOT pinned: the repository under test is built from source at the buggy commit, so the installed pandas version is irrelevant
Cython and build-time numpy must match what pyproject.toml requires at 23f61296bcbf because --no-build-isolation is used; the exact versions are unknown from the evidence

strategy.test_command: python -m pytest pandas/tests/tools/test_to_datetime.py pandas/tests/tools/test_to_timedelta.py -k uint64 -q -p no:cacheprovider
strategy.reproducing_test: pandas/tests/tools/test_to_datetime.py::TestToDatetime::test_uint64_to_datetime_raise_oob and pandas/tests/tools/test_to_timedelta.py::TestToTimedelta::test_uint64_to_timedelta_raise_oob (the scalar-raise assertions are the decisive ones); also test_uint64_to_datetime_coerce and test_uint64_to_timedelta_coerce
strategy.success_criterion: Buggy revision: the uint64 raise tests fail because the scalar to_datetime(uint64_max, unit='ns') and to_timedelta(uint64_max, unit='ns') return a value without raising (DID NOT RAISE), and the coerce tests fail because the scalar result is not NaT. Fixed revision: all uint64 tests pass, with OutOfBoundsDatetime/OutOfBoundsTimedelta raised, coerce yielding NaT, and valid uint64 passthrough equal to the int64 result. The transition is FAIL on buggy and PASS on fixed.
strategy.numerical_probe: python -c "import numpy as np, pandas as pd; print(pd.to_datetime(np.iinfo(np.uint64).max, unit='ns'))"  (buggy: prints 1969-12-31 23:59:59.999999999; fixed: raises OutOfBoundsDatetime)

input_output_examples.expected_output: equal to to_timedelta of the int64-cast array

risks: Platform: the wraparound is a plain uint64-to-int64 cast and should reproduce on any 64-bit Linux or macOS build. No sanitizer or 32-bit platform is implied by the evidence, but the evidence does not confirm this either.

Message regexes in the test diff are unverified: the strings 'cannot convert input with unit ns', 'Out of bounds nanosecond timestamp', and the Timedelta regex 'Cannot cast .* from ns to ns without overflow' may not match the real error text at 23f61296bcbf. If they mismatch, the fixed revision will also fail, and the transition will not be clean.

The array to_datetime path may already raise on the buggy revision (the issue says the list form raises), so the array assertion may pass before the fix. The scalar assertions are the ones that actually transition.
Cython and build-time numpy versions are not stated in the evidence. An incompatible Cython under --no-build-isolation can make the build fail before any test runs.
Numpy 2.2.1 is era-inferred from an issue's installed-version output, not a documented constraint. Results may differ on other NumPy versions, and this is the only pin that is not documented.

The environment lists 'pip install .' as an installation command, but the editable build with --no-build-isolation is the one needed for in-tree tests. Running both can waste time or leave an inconsistent install.
Compiler toolchain (gcc or clang with C and C++ support) is required for the Cython build and is not listed in the evidence, so it is an assumed prerequisite.

oracle.why: The tests use pytest.raises for exceptions and tm.assert_index_equal / 'is NaT' for values, so the oracle is exact equality and exception type, with no numerical tolerance.

strategy.fails_on_buggy: The scalar pytest.raises(OutOfBoundsDatetime) and pytest.raises(OutOfBoundsTimedelta) calls see a returned wrapped timestamp or timedelta instead of an exception, so pytest reports DID NOT RAISE. The coerce tests also fail because the scalar result is not pd.NaT.
strategy.passes_on_fixed: With the fix raising OutOfBoundsTimedelta in _ints_to_td64ns before astype(np.int64), and the analogous to_datetime check in place, the scalar and array raise assertions match, the coerce results are NaT, and the valid passthrough equals the int64 result. Pass depends on the message regexes matching the real messages.
